question:
A 43-year-old woman hospitalized for NSTEMI develops fever and abdominal pain on the third day of
her stay, which has been complicated by multiple factors. Her medical history includes obesity,
coronary artery disease, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, and hypertension. She has a temperature of 37.9°C
(100.3°F), blood pressure of 114/71 mmHg, and a pulse of 111/min. On physical examination, she has
tenderness in the right upper quadrant, and palpation in this area during inspiration causes her to stop
inspiring. She is given intravenous fluids and empiric antibiotics. Laboratory results reveal leukocytosis
with a white blood cell count of 18,100/mm³, while liver function tests and lipase levels are normal. A
diagnostic abdominal ultrasound is ordered and pending. Which of the following ultrasound findings
would most strongly indicate an acalculous disease process? Answer Choices: (A) Gallbladder wall
thickening (>3.5mm) (B) Air within the gallbladder wall (emphysematous cholecystitis) (C)
Pericholecystic fluid (D) Sonographic Murphy sign (E) Absence of gallstones with gallbladder
distension (F) Hepatic abscess adjacent to the gallbladder (G) Dilated common bile duct (H)
Hyperechoic sludge without shadowing (I) Echogenic bile (J) Biliary ductal obstruction without stones
 A. Air within the gallbladder wall (emphysematous cholecystitis)
B. Echogenic bile
C. Hepatic abscess adjacent to the gallbladder
D. Pericholecystic fluid
E. Dilated common bile duct
F. Biliary ductal obstruction without stones
G. Absence of gallstones with gallbladder distension
H. Sonographic Murphy sign
I. Hyperechoic sludge without shadowing
J. Gallbladder wall thickening (>3.5mm)
